types.oie_definition: A nation-state with defined territorial boundaries and a sovereign government.
types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation-state with defined territorial boundaries and a sovereign government. Also called nation, state, country.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Ukraine and Russia are sovereign states, aligning with the Country definition.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

types.oie_definition: A facility where crude oil is processed into refined petroleum products.
types.embedding_query_text: Oil Refinery: A facility where crude oil is processed into refined petroleum products. Also called oil processing plant, petroleum refinery, refinery.

chosen_type.label: OilRefinery
chosen_type.definition: A facility where crude oil is processed into refined petroleum products.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate matches oil refineries; 'Organization' is the closest parent for industrial facilities.

candidates.label: GasStation
candidates.comment: A GasStation is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells fuel for vehicles. Also called petrol station, filling station, service station. Examples: Shell, ExxonMobil, a local independent gas station.

candidates.label: Distillery
candidates.comment: A Distillery is a FoodEstablishment that produces alcoholic beverages through distillation. Also called liquor producer, spirits manufacturer, alcohol plant. Examples: Jack Daniel's Distillery, The Macallan Distillery, Absolut Vodka Distillery. Distinct from Brewery, which produces beer through fermentation.

candidates.label: RecyclingCenter
candidates.comment: A RecyclingCenter is a LocalBusiness providing facilities for recycling waste materials. Also called recycling facility, waste collection center. Examples: a municipal recycling center, a bottle and can redemption center, an electronics recycling drop-off, a hazardous waste collection site.

candidates.label: AutoRepair
candidates.comment: An AutoRepair is an AutomotiveBusiness that provides mechanical maintenance and repair services for vehicles. Also called car mechanic, garage, auto service center, vehicle workshop. Examples: Jiffy Lube, a local independent mechanic, a dealership service department. Distinct from AutoBodyShop, which focuses on exterior and structural damage.

candidates.label: Pharmacy
candidates.comment: A Pharmacy is a local business that dispenses prescription medications and often sells over-the-counter drugs and health products. Also called drugstore, chemist, apothecary. Examples: CVS Pharmacy, Walgreens, a local independent pharmacy. Distinct from Physician, who provides medical consultations.

types.oie_definition: A person holding or seeking a political office in a government.
types.embedding_query_text: Politician: A person holding or seeking a political office in a government. Also called government official, public servant, politician.

chosen_type.label: Politician
chosen_type.definition: A person holding or seeking a political office in a government.
chosen_type.justification: Mentions refer to individuals in political roles; 'Person' is the appropriate parent class.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

types.oie_definition: A subnational division within a country used for governance and administrative purposes.
types.embedding_query_text: Administrative Region: A subnational division within a country used for governance and administrative purposes. Also called province, region, administrative area.

chosen_type.label: AdministrativeArea
chosen_type.justification: Examples like 'Yaroslavl region' and 'Bashkortostan republic' fit as subnational administrative divisions.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

types.oie_definition: A large and permanent human settlement with defined municipal boundaries.
types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement with defined municipal boundaries. Also called urban center, metropolis, city.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Kherson and Odesa are valid city names as per the definition of a permanent human settlement.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.oie_definition: A large saline body of water partially enclosed by land.
types.embedding_query_text: Sea: A large saline body of water partially enclosed by land. Also called ocean, marine area, sea.

chosen_type.label: SeaBodyOfWater
chosen_type.justification: 'Black Sea' is a saline body of water partially enclosed by land, matching SeaBodyOfWater.

candidates.label: SeaBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A large expanse of saltwater, typically part of an ocean or a large inland body of saltwater. Also called sea, ocean, marine body, saltwater expanse. Examples: the Mediterranean Sea, the Caribbean Sea, the Black Sea, the Caspian Sea. Distinct from RiverBodyOfWater, which is a flowing freshwater course.

candidates.label: OceanBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: An OceanBodyOfWater, as a BodyOfWater, is a large expanse of saltwater, such as the Pacific Ocean. Also called ocean, sea, marine body. Examples: Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean. Distinct from LakeBodyOfWater, which is an inland freshwater body.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: LakeBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir. Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.

candidates.label: Pond
candidates.comment: A Pond is a BodyOfWater, typically a small, still body of fresh water. Also called pool, small lake. Examples: a garden pond, a village pond, a duck pond, a natural depression filled with water.

types.oie_definition: A classification of ship or boat based on design or function.
types.embedding_query_text: Vessel Type: A classification of ship or boat based on design or function. Also called ship type, vessel category, marine craft.

chosen_type.label: VesselType
chosen_type.definition: A classification of ship or boat based on design or function.
chosen_type.justification: Mentions like 'Shadow Fleet' and 'dry cargo ships' denote vessel classifications, not terminals or trips.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: BoatTrip
candidates.comment: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

candidates.label: BoatReservation
candidates.comment: A Reservation for travel on a boat, ship, or other water vessel. Also called ferry booking, cruise reservation, boat charter booking. Examples: "A reservation for the Staten Island Ferry", "A booking for a private yacht charter", "A cruise cabin reservation". Distinct from BoatTrip, which describes the journey itself.

types.oie_definition: A count or measure of discrete items or units.
types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A count or measure of discrete items or units. Also called number, amount, quantity.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: Mentions like '11 people' and '93 drones' represent measurable counts, aligning with the Quantity data type.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

types.oie_definition: A specific calendar day in the past or present.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific calendar day in the past or present. Also called calendar date, day, date.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: '5 August' and 'February 2022' are calendar dates without time components, fitting the Date data type.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.oie_definition: A day within the seven-day weekly cycle (e.g., Monday, Tuesday).
types.embedding_query_text: Day of the Week: A day within the seven-day weekly cycle (e.g., Monday, Tuesday). Also called week day, day of the week, weekday.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: HyperTocEntry
candidates.comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

types.oie_definition: An official body responsible for administering specific functions within a government.
types.embedding_query_text: Government Agency: An official body responsible for administering specific functions within a government. Also called public agency, state organization, government body.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.oie_definition: An organization that tracks and analyzes internet connectivity and disruptions.
types.embedding_query_text: Internet Monitoring Group: An organization that tracks and analyzes internet connectivity and disruptions. Also called network watchdog, digital observatory, internet monitoring service.

chosen_type.label: InternetMonitoringGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organization that tracks and analyzes internet connectivity and disruptions.
chosen_type.justification: 'NetBlocks' is an entity monitoring internet outages, requiring a new type under Organization.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: InternetCafe
candidates.comment: An InternetCafe is a local business providing public access to computers with internet connectivity, often alongside food and beverages. Also called cyber cafe, web cafe, net cafe. Examples: a local internet cafe, a gaming cafe with internet access.

candidates.label: TrackAction
candidates.comment: The act of monitoring an inanimate object for updates or changes in its location or status. Also called monitoring, tracking, observing. Examples: tracking a package delivery, monitoring a flight's progress, tracking a lost phone.

candidates.label: OnlineBusiness
candidates.comment: An OnlineBusiness is a particular business that operates primarily or entirely online. Also called e-business, internet business, digital enterprise. Examples: an e-commerce site, an online travel agency, a virtual doctor's office. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which has a physical presence.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

types.oie_definition: A structured group of people with a collective purpose or activity.
types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a collective purpose or activity. Also called institution, group, organization.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: 'BBC Verify' is a structured group with a collective purpose, fitting the Organization definition.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.
